properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Surfaced 2026-08-05 by Anthony's multi-project question.

⚠️ CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. This node first claimed "everything reflow2 has built for crossing a design boundary shares CONTRACTS... NOTHING CARRIES A DECISION OR A REQUIREMENT ACROSS." THAT IS WRONG ABOUT REQUIREMENTS, and it was wrong for the ordinary reason — the claim was made from the capability's one-line description rather than from the code. Reading `export_surface` shows a second, deliberate half: `published_promises()`, behind `req:publishable-promise` (ACCEPTED).

SO THE ACTUAL STATE, verified in `crates/reflow2-core/src/export.rs`: a published surface carries INTERFACES designated `published`, the artifacts that SPECIFY or REALIZE them, REQUIREMENTS the owner designated `published`, and the Project. Everything else is withheld AND COUNTED. Opt-in throughout.

⭐ SO THE REAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN FIRST WRITTEN: WHAT CANNOT CROSS IS THE **DECISION** — the reasoning. A consumer can learn WHAT this design promises and WHERE its boundaries are. It cannot learn WHY.

AND THE MECHANISM FOR THE PARENT DIRECTION ALREADY EXISTS: `cap:derived-completion` is VERIFIED, and `dec:nested-graphs`' second obligation names it — "a parent's view of a composed child must derive from the child's own evidence".

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) NOTHING MORE CROSSES. Defensible and cheapest; the counter is that a sibling re-derives a ruling its neighbour already made. (b) DECISIONS BECOME DESIGNATABLE, the same opt-in shape requirements already have. Small and consistent. Counter, and it is the hard one nobody has answered: IS A MIRRORED DECISION BINDING ON THE MIRRORING DESIGN, OR ONLY VISIBLE TO IT? (c) A STANDING "HOUSE RULES" DESIGN every project mirrors. (d) DO NOT SOLVE IT IN THE GRAPH.

⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THAT BOUNDS ALL OF IT: reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 8 of 72. `publish-surface` and `mirror-surface` are `verified` by their own tests and have barely been exercised on the design that ships them.

THE METHOD NOTE: I asserted an absence from a capability's DESCRIPTION and the code said otherwise. READ THE EXPORT, NOT THE SUMMARY.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
═══ 📌 SHARPENED 2026-08-26 — THE HUB ASKS THIS DOWNWARD, AND THAT ANSWERS (b)'S HARD HALF ═══

Anthony, continuing the hub thread: *"a 'hub' or 'project-brain' repo where leaders/managers can make decisions in and then all the sub-projects inherit those. It kind of allows leaders to work at one level (decision making), while workers operate more in the sub-projects."*

⭐ **AND HE NAMES THE INVERSION HIMSELF, WHICH IS THE CONTRIBUTION:** *"this is somewhat inverse to the hub concept of where all the sub-projects in a hub funnel UP to the hub; whereas what I'm describing here is that the hub funnels DOWN into the sub-projects."*

**That is a different feature from the one `dec:idea-a-hub-owns-designs-it-does-not-absorb-...` describes.** That node's four wants — cross-design realization, sync notification, verification roll-up, last-export-date — all flow UPWARD: status and evidence collecting at the hub. This flows DOWNWARD: **authority distributing from the hub.** Same topology, opposite direction, and they need not be built together or at all.

🛑 **AND IT SETTLES, OR AT LEAST TAKES A SIDE ON, THE QUESTION OPTION (b) COULD NOT ANSWER.** That option's counter was *"IS A MIRRORED DECISION BINDING ON THE MIRRORING DESIGN, OR ONLY VISIBLE TO IT?"* — asked because a Decision that governs nothing on the far side is a note, and one that governs is an authority claim across the boundary the whole rule exists to draw.

**"Leaders decide and sub-projects inherit" is the BINDING reading, said out loud.** It is not a mirrored note; it is governance. That makes the objection sharper rather than softer:

- **A binding cross-design Decision means one design's `GOVERNED_BY` edges point at another design's node.** Nothing in the schema forbids it and nothing supports it — the `parks` ruling, the enforcement flag and `check_intent_authority` all assume the governing Decision is in the same graph, owned by the same person.
- **`check_intent_authority` is the ENFORCED rule** — intent moves only on the owner's word. **Whose word governs a child that inherited a decision it never approved?** The hub owner's, presumably — which is exactly the authority claim, and exactly what makes it a real feature rather than a convenience.
- ⚠️ **And the tracker objection returns in a new costume.** Upward roll-up looks like PPM reporting; downward governance looks like PPM *control*. That is not obviously better, and the existing hub node's counter — *"every step toward being good at that is a step toward being worse at holding WHY"* — applies to both directions.

⭐ **THE COUNTER-COUNTER, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST THING SAID FOR EITHER DIRECTION:** downward inheritance is the one that carries **WHY**. A sub-project inheriting *"we settled that outdoor units send cumulative totals, so a lost reading heals itself"* receives reasoning, not status. **Upward roll-up moves numbers; downward inheritance moves rationale** — and holding WHY is the thing this design says it exists for. If either direction earns its place, the argument for this one is better.

📌 A GENUINELY OPEN SUB-QUESTION NOBODY HAS ASKED: **does an inherited decision keep the hub's id, or get copied?** A copy is a second source of truth (see `dec:idea-the-hub-holds-a-copy-per-sub-repo-and-copies-go-stale`); a reference means the child's graph cannot be read alone, which breaks `dec:nested-graphs`' ownership boundary. Both readings cost something real.



═══ RULED 2026-10-07 BY ANTHONY, FOR REQUIREMENTS FLOWING DOWN (slice 3 of the hub work) ═══
Asked "When a parent's requirement reaches a part, how should it become binding?", he chose "Once accepted" over "Binding on arrival" and "Visible only".
- WHAT CROSSES: requirements. A Decision node does not cross yet; the parent's reasoning travels as text attached to the requirement. Option (b), decisions becoming designatable, stays open.
- BINDING: the requirement lands in the part at `proposed` and binds when the PART's owner accepts it. This answers option (b)'s hard half without putting GOVERNED_BY across a graph boundary, so check_intent_authority keeps its single-owner meaning. Where one person owns both designs, as in the dev_reflow2 hub, they accept with their own word in the same step.
- REFERENCE OR COPY: a copy that records its origin (the parent design, the parent requirement's id and the version it was taken from), so the part's design can still be read alone (dec:nested-graphs) and the copy cannot go stale silently: a moved origin is reported.
- Transport: dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency, ruled the same day.
properties.name: OPEN — decisions cannot cross a design boundary; and the hub case asks it in the DOWNWARD direction, where inheritance is the point
properties.rationale:
Corrected an hour after it was written, on the same day, because the first version asserted an absence it had not checked — and an absence is exactly the kind of claim that hardens into folklore. The correction is kept in the node rather than silently replacing the text so the failure mode stays visible.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this asks WHAT MAY CROSS IT.

SHARPENED 2026-08-26. The hub thread asks this question in the DOWNWARD direction — leaders decide, sub-projects inherit — and that is recorded here rather than as a new node because it is the same question with a direction attached, and because it takes a side on option (b)'s unanswered half: inheritance means BINDING, not merely visible. Splitting it would separate an answer from the question it answers.

What the sharpening adds beyond direction: binding inheritance puts `GOVERNED_BY` across a graph boundary, which `check_intent_authority` — the one ENFORCED rule here — has no account of, since it assumes governor and governed share an owner. That is the concrete obstacle, and it was not visible while the question was asked in the abstract.
